content.text:
The pattern matches NaVO2 (mp-19391) alone.

1. **Main peaks:** I simulated NaVO2. The observed strong peaks line up with it in both position and relative height. The low-angle peak near 16.3° is about 73 observed against 71 simulated. The pair near 41–42° is 100 and 51 observed against 100 and 49 simulated. The medium peaks near 31–33°, 35.8° and the 58–64° group also match.
2. **Weak peaks:** The smaller peaks at higher angle also line up with NaVO2, so no unexplained peaks are left that would need a second phase.
3. **CrCuO2 ruled out:** I also simulated CrCuO2 (mp-510625), another layered oxide with the same space group (166). Its strongest peak falls at a different angle from the observed 100% peak, so it is not present.

I did not simulate the other seven candidates, because NaVO2 on its own already accounts for every significant peak.

{"present": ["mp-19391"], "confidence": 0.95, "note": "The simulated NaVO2 pattern matches all main observed peaks, about 16.3, 31-36, 41-42 and 58-64 degrees, with matching relative intensities and nothing left unexplained."}
